questions.question_prompt: After a long motorway drive, 60 km/h feels unusually slow. What should you do?
questions.keyed_answer: Check the speedometer and adapt to the new road conditions.
questions.teaching_excerpt: After a long period at a steady motorway speed, your perception can adapt to that pace. On a slower road, the correct lower speed may feel unusually slow. This effect is often called speed adaptation or velocitation. Check the speedometer regularly to judge actual speed and adjust to the current limit and conditions. The feeling alone is not evidence that the speedometer is faulty. ODOT: speed perception and speedometer checks Worked transition. After a long motorway trip, you leave onto a road signed 50 km/h. At 50, the car feels as if it is crawling. Confirm the speedometer reading, read the new road and retain a speed suited to its limit, visibility and hazards. Do not accelerate merely to recover the motorway's familiar feeling.
questions.coverage_reasoning: Explains steady-speed perceptual adaptation, deceptive slow feeling, speedometer checks, current limit/conditions and motorway-to-50 example. Feeling alone does not establish instrument fault.

questions.question_prompt: Heavy traffic makes a country-road left turn unsafe. What is a sensible alternative?
questions.keyed_answer: Continue to a suitable turning place and return for a right turn.
questions.teaching_excerpt: On an ordinary two-way rural road, heavy traffic may make a direct left turn unsafe. Continue to a suitable, permitted place or route where you can change direction safely, then return to approach the destination with a right turn if that movement is allowed and safe. This can avoid hazardous waiting and crossing the opposing stream at the original entrance. It is a planning alternative, not permission to turn around immediately on the carriageway. If no safe legal return route exists, choose another route or postpone. Trafikverket: example of routing to a turning place Legal boundary. Before turning or leaving the road, protect oncoming traffic and traffic on the road you enter; take particular care of following traffic. A turnaround must cause neither danger nor obstruction. Signs and access restrictions still apply. Never turn around or reverse on a motorway or expressway. If you can wait safely and legally for a left turn, remember the advice in M04-L02 to keep the front wheels straight; that advice does not make an unsafe turn suitable. Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§24, 26, 29 and 46; chapter 9 §§1–2 Worked rural alternative. A farm entrance is on your left and busy traffic leaves no safe opportunity. You continue to an accessible junction route that legally and safely brings you back in the opposite direction. The entrance is then on your right. Check people, traffic and the entrance again before turning; the revised route does not guarantee a safe final movement. Wil

questions.question_prompt: When is extra attention to large animals especially important?
questions.keyed_answer: Around dusk and dawn near wildlife habitats and fence openings.
questions.teaching_excerpt: Give extra attention at dawn and dusk, near animal habitats and where fences end or have openings. Scan woodland edges, bushes and small waterways beside the road: Trafikverket's road-project study describes these as animal routes that can conceal an approach. Its national guidance also describes animal passages through fence openings. These are cues for observation and speed planning, not predictions that animals only cross there. Trafikverket: wildlife and fence passages · Trafikverket: habitat example, page 9 Apply the cues. At dusk, woodland meets a field beside a gap in the fence. Read the edges and opening as possible animal approaches, and choose speed for the view and foreseeable hazard. Keep observing even on fenced stretches. Prevention belongs here; actions after a collision are in M10-L01.
questions.coverage_reasoning: Explicit dawn/dusk, habitat edges/bushes/waterways and fence endings/openings, with observation and speed-planning example; year-round uncertainty retained and post-collision instructions cross-linked to M10.
